# linbpq

**BPQ32 packet-radio node, BBS and Winlink gateway**

- **Version recorded:** 25.39
- **Categories:** `emcomm`, `packet`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/g8bpq/LinBPQ>

## What it does

Runs a packet-radio node: a switch that relays AX.25 traffic between RF ports and the internet, with an integrated BBS, a Winlink RMS gateway, chat, and APRS support. It is the software behind a large share of the packet nodes still on the air.

## Why you would want it

If you want to operate infrastructure rather than just use it — host a BBS, provide a Winlink gateway for your area, or link a local packet network to the wider one — this is the standard implementation. It has no real alternative on Linux.

## Before it will work

A configured AX.25 stack, a TNC or soundmodem such as Direwolf or QtSoundModem, and a callsign in `/etc/bpq32.cfg`. Running a Winlink gateway additionally requires registration with the Winlink system.

## How it installs

- git (make) — https://github.com/g8bpq/LinBPQ at `25.39`
  - build dependencies: `build-essential`, `libpaho-mqtt-dev`, `libjansson-dev`, `libminiupnpc-dev`, `libconfig-dev`, `libpcap-dev`, `zlib1g-dev`, `libi2c-dev`
  - the project's build system has no install rule; the binaries listed below are copied into the prefix instead
  - Dependency list derived from the LIBS line of upstream's makefile (-lpaho-mqtt3a -ljansson -lminiupnpc -lm -lz -lpthread -lconfig -lpcap) and verified present on Debian 13 by querying the target container, not by guessing package names. Upstream supports `make noi2c` to drop the I2C dependency on hardware without it.

Binaries this produces:

- `linbpq`

## What it changes on your machine

- **group_membership** — LinBPQ needs serial and audio access for TNCs and soundmodems
  - adds the operating user to the `dialout` group
  - undo: gpasswd -d <user> dialout

## Configuration it writes

- `/etc/bpq32.cfg` (mode 0644, existing file backed up)

## Known problems

Upstream publishes prebuilt binaries in a directory named Beta with no versioning or checksums; we ignore those and build from a tagged source revision instead. The generated configuration is a minimum viable node and is meant to be edited — read it before transmitting.

## Keeping it current

- probe: github tags (`g8bpq/LinBPQ`)
- strategy: rebuild
- Upstream tags frequently and cuts no GitHub releases — 25.39, 25.36, 25.35 within one year. Tag selection is a stability judgement, not "take latest".
